description: The >>CALL-CONVENTION {COBOL | convention-name} compiler directive (ISO §2023:7.3.9) - it associates a convention-name with a set of implementor-defined call conventions for CALL/INVOKE and the ENTRY convention. Recognized and consumed by the text-manipulation stage; WiseOwl COBOL defines no call-convention-name, so >>CALL-CONVENTION COBOL is the only accepted form and its no-op disposition is faithful (any other word is COBOL1911, kb/Work PB1383); the introduction gate rejects the directive word below 2002. The §2023:7.3 compiler-directive facility is a COBOL-2002 introduction: COBOL-85 has no compiler directives at all, so a '>>' line cannot occur in a conforming COBOL-85 source. The edition edge below 2023 is DERIVED, not quoted (VCR Table 7's discipline, rows 7.19/7.20 - the repo holds no 2002 or 2014 text, ratified decision #1): the derivation is (a) the M2 post-85 feature catalog in docs/ISO2023_CONFORMANCE_PLAN.md, which places '*>' inline comments, >>SOURCE FORMAT, conditional compilation and 'recognize-and-ignore of the other standard >> directives' in COBOL-2002, (b) the sibling row leap-second-directive-2002, already landed on the same derivation (kb/Work PB65), and (c) Annex E, which itemizes the 2014->2023 delta and does NOT list this directive among the additions, so it predates 2023. Overturnable in one line if the 2002/2014 text is ever acquired.
citation: ISO §2023:7.3.9; the §2023:7.3 compiler-directive facility is a COBOL-2002 introduction (M2 catalog derivation, VCR Table 7 discipline)

directiveOperand.citation: ISO §2023:7.3.9.2 general format: { COBOL | call-convention-name-1 }, plain braces — exactly one shall be written; call-convention-name-1 names one of the implementor's call conventions (§2023:7.3.9.3 GR2 b) maps program-names under it 'in a manner defined by the implementor'), and WiseOwl COBOL defines none, so COBOL is the whole admissible set and any other word names no convention.

source:
>>CALL-CONVENTION COBOL
       IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
       PROGRAM-ID. PB725CC.
       PROCEDURE DIVISION.
       MAIN.
           DISPLAY "X".
           STOP RUN.
